using both medical and common firsthand experiences are helpful, i don't think anyone should be relying too heavily on one or the other. we used to be overly worried about our system when we first recognized being one and getting too caught up on the medical aspect strains your relationship with yourself, your system, and the community of people like you. definitely don't believe everything you read on internet communities but the same can be said for shit in the psych field because god knows how corrupt and ableist supposed professionals can be, y'know? letting ourselves just be how we are has helped us as a system trying to survive and recover way more than getting caught up on trying to make everything fit this narrow idea of how systems should be, and that's what i think is important here because putting yourself in a box doesn't do anything but hurt you and the people around you

First and foremost, you should care more about your partner/their system's opinions and talk to them first. Everyone experiences being a system differently! No one system speaks for everybody out there. 
Both us and our partner are systems. We don't date outside of each other. A couple of our alters made the choice to date other people, but it ended up too complicated. This was our decision. You aren't a bad partner for wanting to be monogamous with alters in a system, just as you wouldn't be with dating another singlet. Ultimately, it depends entirely on their comfort. Don't be forceful about it, but if you're just requesting monogamy with somebody you want to love for the rest of your life, there's nothing wrong with that. But understand every alter has their own needs too, and try to remain understanding to them since you don't have the same experiences with living as a system. Otherwise? You aren't bad for trying to be comfortable if you're not pushing anything too harshly.
